title: Kitchen Lab recipe evidence
scope: Illustrative recipe simulation; not a validated predictor of real cooking temperatures or times. Written explanations require human review.

explanations.question: Why did adding pasta lower the water temperature?
Why can a crowded, wet pan delay mushroom browning?
explanations.answer: The released water keeps the cooking surface wet.

findings.label: Recipe portion measured
findings.observation: 160 g weighed for 2 servings; recipe target 160 g.
findings.nextPractice: Keep weighing against the scaled recipe before cooking.

findings.label: Pasta checked and slightly firm
findings.observation: Finished pasta: Tender with a slight bite. Last sample: Tender with a slight bite. Pasta was stirred in the pot.
findings.nextPractice: Keep using a fresh sample and allow for the time spent finishing in the pan.

findings.label: Mushrooms golden, without scorching
findings.observation: Golden, glossy mushrooms. Standard pan with 200 g of mushrooms.
findings.nextPractice: Keep watching color as moisture escapes; lower the heat once golden.

findings.label: Sauce coats the pasta
findings.observation: 50 mL modeled sauce moisture; 50 mL reserved water added, 150 mL left in the jug.
findings.nextPractice: Keep adding saved water in small amounts and checking the coating.

findings.label: Dish checked; both burners off
findings.observation: Final dish checked; pot burner off, pan burner off.
findings.nextPractice: Keep checking after your last adjustment and turning both burners off before plating.
